info.title: AXLR Bots activity audit
info.description: The input adapter that watches the fleet's activity and turns each new kind of failure in a finished task into one event for the QA team (the pattern is docs/architecture/input-adapters.md). Deterministic: no model. It long-polls each team's timeline through the control plane's socket (`GET /v1/groups/{name}/events?after=&wait=30s`) as a wake-up; on a task's end (`bot.task.completed`, `bot.task.failed`, `bot.task.expired`, `bot.task.cancelled`) it reads the task (`GET /v1/tasks/{id}`), its executions (`GET /v1/tasks/{id}/executions`, the result's `toolCalls`) and its timeline (`GET /v1/tasks/{id}/events`, the `bot.task.progress` items `tool.started` and `tool.ended` that carry a call's cut summary and its error's first line). Each failed call, and a failed task's reason, is normalised into a signature; a signature it has not seen is published once, as `actividad.fallo`, to team `qa` as the operator (`POST /v1/groups/{team}/events`). The signatures it has seen are its own file, `<state>/activity-audit/seen.json`, described here as `SeenFile` so that no DTO of the package is written by hand. The wire forms are `adapters/activityaudit`; the runbook is docs/runbooks/activity-audit.md.

controlPlane.description: The control plane's operator API over its Unix socket (<state>/axlr-bots.sock): the adapter reads the timelines and publishes as the operator, at depth 0.

teamEvents.title: The QA team's events
teamEvents.description: The operator API's publish route (docs/reference/operator-api.md). A signature names its idempotency key, so a publish repeated after a crash answers the event published before and delivers nothing twice.

team.description: The team the adapter publishes to: --team, qa by default.

sendActividadFallo.summary: A task ended with a failure whose signature the adapter has not published: one actividad.fallo. A signature it published before grows its count in the seen-store and publishes nothing. At most --per-minute (6) a minute, oldest first, so a first --since backfill does not flood QA.

actividadFallo.name: actividad.fallo
actividadFallo.title: A new kind of failure in the fleet's activity

ActividadFalloEvent.description: The operator API's publish body (application.PublishGroupEventCommand) for actividad.fallo. Its kind is info (a domain-style name): the QA members that subscribe to it hear it.

message.description: One line that stands on its own (a coalesced note or a redelivery carries only it and data.id): `<id> · <tool> · <bot> (<team>) · <program or -> · <error>`, cut to 280 characters. A failed task's tool is `task`; a bridged call's program is the plugin's tool it reached; a bot in no team is `(-)`.
examples: fallo-ebbdaebc51f616fa · axlr_remember · dev-go (dev) · - · send the continuation alone to commit a reviewed write

idempotencyKey.description: activity:<signature id>; activity:<signature id>:r<n> after the n-th --rearm of it. The control plane names an operator's event by its key and its body: the body is fixed when the signature falls due (SeenSignature.due), so a retry is the same event.

id.description: The signature: fallo- and 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of its key; within [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}.

kind.description: tool_call: a call that ended failed; task_failed: a task that ended Failed.

bot.description: The bot of the occurrence that published it.

team.description: The bot's team, when it is in one.

tool.description: The runtime's tool, for a tool_call.

program.description: For local_exec, the program's basename, when the call's summary shows it whole.

mcp_tool.description: For axlr_call_tool, the plugin's tool it reached (plugin/tool).

error.description: The error's first line, normalised (ids, shas, times, paths under /home, numbers and quoted text replaced, secrets redacted), at most 400 characters. Never the call's output.

partial.description: True when the run's line was cut before what the signature needs (the program, the exit code, the error): the bot stands in for the program in the signature.

count.description: The occurrences seen up to the publish (a backfill can give more than 1 at the first event); the seen-store keeps counting after it, for the report.

first_at.description: When it was first seen (the call's end, or the task's), RFC 3339.

SeenFile.description: The adapter's own file, <state>/activity-audit/seen.json, written atomically: the signatures seen and the tasks audited.

cursor.description: The creation time from which the next reconciliation lists tasks: the oldest task still unfinished at the last one, else the newest seen. RFC 3339.

tasks.description: The tasks audited whose creation is not older than the cursor: a task is audited once.

key.description: What was hashed: the parts of the failure that make its kind.

recovered.description: The occurrences after which the same call succeeded later in the same task.

bots.description: The bots it was seen from, sorted.

last_bot.description: The bot of the newest occurrence: the one an event names.

last_task.description: The task of the newest occurrence.

published_at.description: When actividad.fallo was published for it; absent while it has not been.

event_id.description: The event the control plane answered.

DuePublish.description: What the event of a signature says, fixed when it fell due and kept before it is published: a publish retried after a crash, or after the control plane refused it, is the same body under the same key, so the control plane answers the event it published before.
